claims.text: High configurational entropy promotes a nanoscale, uniform distribution of oxidation-active elements in high-entropy alloys.
Cr, Al, and Ti are oxidation-active elements with high oxygen affinity.
Uniformly distributed oxidation-active elements selectively oxidize during high-temperature exposure.
Selective oxidation produces a continuous and adherent protective oxide scale.
HEA matrices possess intrinsically sluggish diffusion kinetics.
Sluggish matrix diffusion limits oxide-scale thickening and spallation.
Limiting oxide growth and spallation allows long-term oxidation resistance to be retained.
The target material is a near-equiatomic or compositionally tailored HEA containing at least one oxidation-active element and having a largely single-phase, homogeneous microstructure.
The proposed mechanism is applicable during oxidation in air or another oxidizing atmosphere at approximately 800–900 °C.
A continuous oxide film acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
Sluggish diffusion retards both outward transport of alloying elements and inward transport of oxygen.
Retarded elemental and oxygen transport stabilizes the protective oxide scale.
Relative to a compositionally similar but segregated alloy, the uniformly distributed HEA will have a lower oxidation rate and lower mass gain.
Relative to the segregated baseline, the uniformly distributed HEA will form a denser, more continuous, and more adherent oxide scale.
The uniformly distributed HEA will retain its protective scale for longer than the segregated baseline.
The mechanism requires a sufficient concentration of oxidation-active elements and may fail when their content is insufficient or alternative oxidation pathways dominate.
The controlled comparison uses samples with identical bulk chemistry but different degrees of nanoscale elemental uniformity, oxidized in static air at 850 °C for 100 hours.
Failure of the uniform samples to show lower mass gain or a more continuous and adherent scale than the segregated controls is specified as a falsifying outcome.
